q: Which is best for cutting curves on wood?
n: A jigsaw is best for cutting curves in wood. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (woodworking tools); manufacturer tool guides.

q: A saw which uses a reciprocating blade to cut irregular curves.
n: A jigsaw uses a reciprocating blade to cut irregular curves. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (woodworking tools); manufacturer tool guides.

q: A power saw using a toothed or abrasive disc to cut different materials using a rotary motion spinning around an arbor. It can be hand-held or mounted on a machine.
n: A circular saw uses a toothed or abrasive disc spinning on an arbor. It can be hand-held or machine-mounted. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (woodworking tools); manufacturer tool guides.

q: Also known as a cut-off saw, it is used to make crosscuts. It cannot make angles, bevels, curves nor rip cuts.
n: A chop (cut-off) saw makes straight crosscuts only, with no angles, bevels, curves or rip cuts. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (woodworking tools); manufacturer tool guides.

q: It is used to make crosscuts and rip cuts. Since it is mounted, it is stable and safer to use. The operator pushes the stock into the blade to make the cut, and a guide helps maintain a straight cut parallel to the blade.
n: A table saw is mounted and stable. The stock is pushed through the blade along a rip fence for straight crosscuts and rip cuts. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (woodworking tools); manufacturer tool guides.

q: It is used to make accurate crosscuts as well as beveled cuts. Its stand can pivot left and right, usually to a maximum angle of 45 degrees.
n: A miter saw makes accurate crosscuts and angled cuts. Its table pivots left and right, usually up to 45°. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (woodworking tools); manufacturer tool guides.

q: It is a versatile woodworking tool used for precise crosscuts and a variety of angled cuts. The stand holding it can pivot left and right, usually to a maximum angle of 45 degrees.
n: The miter saw is the tool for precise crosscuts and angled (miter) cuts, pivoting up to about 45°. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (woodworking tools); manufacturer tool guides.

q: Identify the cladding material chosen for high-humidity regions because it resists rot, termites, and moisture while still imitating painted wood lap siding. It is commonly paired with stone bases in tropical residential construction.
n: Fiber cement board resists rot, termites and moisture while imitating painted wood lap siding, so it suits humid regions. Source: ASTM C1186 (fiber-cement flat sheets); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Identify the lightweight, color-integrated polymer siding widely used in mass-housing projects due to its low cost, rapid installation, and minimal maintenance requirements.
n: Vinyl siding is light, colored through, cheap and quick to install, which is why mass housing uses it. Source: ASTM D3679 (rigid PVC siding).

q: Identify the wood-based cladding profile with a recessed channel that creates deep horizontal shadow lines. It is preferred in resort-style architecture for its natural grain and warm appearance.
n: Channel wood plank siding has a recessed channel that casts deep horizontal shadow lines, a warm natural look for resort architecture. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood siding profiles).

q: Identify the hollow-core polymer siding used in coastal environments for its corrosion resistance, bright finish, and ability to maintain appearance without repainting.
n: Hollow-core PVC siding resists corrosion near the coast and keeps its bright finish without repainting. Source: ASTM D3679.

q: Identify the facade system composed of flat metallic panels bonded to a polymer core, used in commercial buildings to achieve crisp joints, large spans, and a modern geometric appearance.
n: Aluminum composite panels (two thin aluminum skins on a polymer core) give crisp joints, large flat spans and a modern geometric look. Source: AAMA 508 (ACM systems); NFPA 285.

q: Identify the cladding material combining wood fibers and thermoplastic resin, installed with tight joints and embossed grain to achieve a modern, termite-resistant facade without the maintenance burden of real wood.
n: WPC panels combine wood fiber and thermoplastic resin, with embossed grain, for termite-resistant, low-maintenance cladding. Source: ASTM D7032.

q: A luxury wellness spa is constructing a feature wall that must produce true sculptural depth, with surfaces that physically project outward to form continuous waves and parametric contours. The designer specifies a finish that is non-structural, used strictly for interior accent walls. and typically manufactured from PVC, gypsum, plant fiber. or CNC-routed MDF. During installation, the contractor must prepare a perfectly flat substrate, apply construction adhesive or gypsum-based adhesive, align panels using a laser level, and then treat the joints with acrylic filler or joint compound to create a seamless, continuous pattern. Based on this description, identify the material being referred to.
n: 3D wall panels (PVC, gypsum, plant fiber or CNC-routed MDF) make sculptural, non-structural interior feature walls. They are glued to a flat substrate and the joints filled for a seamless pattern. Source: Manufacturer installation guides (3D decorative wall panels).

q: A logistics company in Subic Bay Freeport is constructing a new industrial warehouse that must maintain stable interior temperatures despite intense coastal heat and high humidity. The project requires a wall and roof system that provides structural rigidity, thermal insulation, and rapid installation over a steel framing grid. The specified material must consist of two pre-painted metal skins bonded to an insulated core such as EPS, PU, PIR, or rockwool, and must be installed using self-tapping screws, butyl tape, and interlocking joints to create a sealed, high-performance building envelope suitable for industrial operations. Which material best fits this description?
n: Sandwich panels have two pre-painted metal skins bonded to an insulating core (EPS, PU, PIR or rockwool). They are screwed to steel framing with interlocking, taped joints. Source: EN 14509 (self-supporting double-skin metal faced insulating panels).

q: A quality assurance certification used in the metals industry to quantify the chemical and physical properties of a metal product.
n: A mill certificate (mill test report) certifies the chemical and physical properties of a metal product. Source: EN 10204 (inspection documents); ASTM A6.

q: If you want to avoid or minimize staining, which countertop will you recommend?
n: Engineered quartz is non-porous and resists staining better than travertine, marble or granite. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (stone); ASTM C615/C503/C568; manufacturer data.

q: A high-end residential kitchen is designed for heavy culinary use, including frequent exposure to acidic ingredients such as citrus, vinegar, wine reduction, and tomato-based sauces. The client demands a countertop material that will not stain even when spills are left unattended, and will not etch, dull, or discolor when exposed to repeated acidic contact. The surface must also maintain its appearance under intense cleaning cycles using strong household detergents. Which material is most appropriate for this application?
n: Sintered stone is non-porous and acid- and chemical-resistant. It will not stain, etch or dull under acidic foods and strong detergents. Source: ISO 10545 (ceramic tile chemical resistance); manufacturer data.

q: A designer is evaluating several finish materials for a kitchen renovation in Manila, where resistance to staining and moisture absorption is a major concern duc to the humid summer climate. The client wants to avoid any material that absorbs liquids easily or requires frequent sealing. Among the following options, which material naturally exhibits the highest porosity and therefore the greatest tendency to absorb liquids?
n: Marble is the most porous of these, so it absorbs liquids and needs sealing. Source: ASTM C503 (marble absorption); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (stone); ASTM C615/C503/C568.

q: From among the choices, which would you recommend for swimming pools and toilets?
n: Glass mosaic is impervious and chemical-resistant, the usual choice for pools and toilets. Source: ANSI A137.2 (glass tile).

q: For the answer in the previous item, which material will you use to fill the gap between the mosaic tiles?
n: Grout is the cementitious or epoxy filler worked into the joints between tiles, such as mosaic tiles. It locks the tiles together and seals the joints against water and dirt. Source: ANSI A118.6/A118.7 (grouts).

q: An architect is selecting a natural stone finish for the exterior steps and lobby flooring of a premium office tower in Bonifacio Globa City. The client insists on using granite duc to its reputation for long-term durability, Which set of characterisiies correctly describes granite and justifies its suitability for this application?
o: Very hard, high compressive strength, low porosity, excellent abrasion and weather resistance
Highly porous, grainy texture, prone to surface flaking under heavy traffic
Soft, easily scratched, high porosity, sensitive to acids and staining
Lightweight, low density, suitable only for decorative interior wall cladding
n: Granite is very hard, with high compressive strength, low porosity and excellent abrasion and weather resistance. Source: ASTM C615 (granite dimension stone).

q: A project requires a stone with large, visible mineral crystals, excellent compressive strength, and high resistance to abrasion, commonly used for steps, exterior cladding, and polished lobby floors. The architect identifies the material as granite, which forms from the slow cooling of magma beneath the Earth's surface. How is this rock classified?
n: Granite is an igneous (intrusive) rock, formed from magma cooling slowly underground. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (stone); ASTM C615/C503/C568; geology references.

q: A hotel lobby finish requires a stone that can be cut into slabs, accepts a high polish, and displays recrystallized calcite veins resulting from the transformation of limestone under heat and pressure. The architect identifies the material as marble. How is this stone classified?
n: Marble is a metamorphic rock: limestone recrystallized under heat and pressure. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (stone); ASTM C615/C503/C568.

q: A heritage restoration project requires a stone that can be easily carved. exhibits fine to coarse calcite grains, and reacts visibly with weak acids due to its high calcium carbonate content. The material must also be suitable as a primary raw ingredient in Portland cement production and commonly used as aggregate in concrete. Which sedimentary rock best fits these characteristics?
n: Limestone is mostly calcium carbonate. It carves easily, fizzes with weak acid, and is the main raw material for Portland cement and a common aggregate. Source: ASTM C568 (limestone dimension stone); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (stone); ASTM C615/C503/C568.

q: A materials engineer is evaluating potential quarry sources for a cement manufacturing facility in Bulacan. The plant requires a sedimentary rock that 1s abundant, easy to process, and serves as the primary raw material for producing clinker. Which sedimentary rock is most commonly used in construction for this purpose?
n: Limestone is the abundant sedimentary rock that is the main raw material for cement clinker. Source: ASTM C150; Neville, Properties of Concrete, Ch. 1.

q: An architect wants to minimize stormwater runoll by using a paving material that permits water infiltration. Which material is most appropriate?
n: Brick pavers laid with open joints on a permeable base let water soak in, cutting runoff. Source: ICPI Permeable Interlocking Concrete Pavements; US EPA stormwater BMPs.

q: From among the choices, which is the most suitable for an outdoor playground?
n: Rubber pavers cushion falls and resist slipping, which suits playgrounds. Source: ASTM F1292 (impact attenuation); CPSC Public Playground Safety Handbook.

q: Which concrete finish creates textured ridges that improve traction, making surfaces safer when wet and improving slip resistance?
n: A broom finish is made by dragging a stiff broom across fresh concrete. The ridges it leaves improve traction and slip resistance when wet. Source: Kosmatka et al., Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures (PCA), Ch. 15 (Finishing).

q: Which concrete finish is applied while the surface is still workable, uses rubber stamp mats to imprint textures, and is primarily used to replicate the appearance of stone, brick, slate or wood at a lower cost?
n: Stamped concrete is imprinted with rubber stamp mats while still workable, to imitate stone, brick, slate or wood at lower cost. Source: Kosmatka et al., Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures (PCA), Ch. 15 (Decorative Finishes).

q: Which concrete finish uses disposable paper or plastic templates to simulate decorative patterns like brick, tile or stone on flat surfaces, and can be applied to fresh or hardened concrete using spray-on overlays?
n: Stencil concrete uses disposable paper or plastic templates, often with spray-on overlays, to create brick, tile or stone patterns on fresh or hardened concrete. It is easy to apply and modify. Source: Kosmatka et al., Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures (PCA), Ch. 15 (Decorative Finishes).

q: Which flooring finish is a composite material of decorative aggregates like marble, quartz or glass embedded in a cementitious or epoxy binder, ground and polished to a smooth, glossy surface after curing, and is known for its long lifespan and minimal maintenance needs?
n: Terrazzo is decorative aggregate (marble, quartz, glass) set in a cement or epoxy binder, then ground and polished after curing. It is durable and low-maintenance. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 10 (Terrazzo Flooring); National Terrazzo & Mosaic Association.

q: A contractor is preparing the interior walls of a two-bedroom residence in Cebu City. The total paintable wall area after deducting doors and windows is 148 square meters. The architect specifies a latex paint to be used as the primer. If the paint covers 8 sqm/liter for one coat over the given surface area, how many 4-liter cans should be purchased to complete the priming works?
n: Paint needed = 148 sqm / 8 sqm per liter = 18.5 liters. Cans = 18.5 / 4 = 4.6, rounded up to 5 cans of 4 liters. Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Painting Works); paint manufacturer spreading-rate data.

q: A facilities team is selecting a coating for metal door frames in a high-traffic corridor. The specification requires a paint that uses a resin binder, forms a hard and durable enamel-type film, and dries significantly faster than traditional oil-based coatings to minimize downtime during operations. Which paint type best satisfies these requirements?
n: Catalyzed (two-component) coatings cure by a chemical reaction between the resin and a hardener. They form a hard, durable, enamel-like film much faster than air-dried oil or alkyd paints, so downtime is short. Source: Steel Structures Painting Council (SSPC) Painting Manual, Vol. 2 (Catalyzed Coatings); ASTM D16.

q: Which paint will you specify for an interior ceiling?
n: Latex (water-based) paint is the usual specification for interior ceilings. It is low-odor, dries quickly, has a flat sheen that hides imperfections, and cleans up with water. Source: PDCA Painting Standards; Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Finishes).

q: Which is the most appropriate topcoat paint material for the concrete exterior of a 3-level detached residence?
n: Elastomeric paint forms a thick, flexible film that stretches over hairline cracks and resists wind-driven rain. That makes it the topcoat of choice for exterior concrete walls in the tropics. Source: ASTM D6904 (Wind-Driven Rain Resistance of Masonry Coatings); PDCA Painting Standards.

q: A paint with high sheen which can be used at the exterior
n: Semi-gloss has a high sheen yet weathers well. It is washable and moisture-resistant, so it is used on exterior trim, doors and walls. Flat latex has no sheen. Source: Master Painters Institute (MPI) Gloss and Sheen Standards; PDCA Painting Standards.

q: Paint for high-traffic areas
n: The higher the gloss, the harder and more washable the film, so glossy finishes suit high-traffic areas that get scuffs and frequent cleaning. Source: Master Painters Institute (MPI) Gloss and Sheen Standards; PDCA Painting Standards.

q: Paint applied on steel columns that acts as insulation and expands when in contact with fire
n: Intumescent paint swells into a thick, insulating char when heated. This slows the temperature rise of steel members and raises their fire-resistance rating. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (fire-resistive coatings); ASTM E119 / UL 263 fire-resistance testing.

q: A painter applies an excessively thick coat of paint on a vertical concrete wall. Before the coating fully dries, the paint film begins to flow downward, creating uneven drips, curtains and wavy streaks on the surface. What is this paint defect called?
n: Sagging (runs and curtains) happens when a coat is applied too thick, or the paint is over-thinned, on a vertical surface. The wet film flows down under gravity before it sets. Source: ASTM D4414 (Wet Film Thickness); PDCA Painting Standards (Paint Film Defects).

q: Size of coarse aggregate commonly used for slabs on grade
n: Slabs on grade commonly use 3/4-inch (19 mm) crushed gravel. It is easy to place and finish in a 100 mm slab, and the maximum aggregate size stays well under one-third of the slab thickness. Source: ACI 302.1R (Concrete Floor and Slab Construction); ASTM C33 Size No. 67.

q: During site grading, a stockpile of clean, angular construction gravel is delivered and dumped on a compacted base course. Assuming the aggregate is dry, free-draining, and composed primarily of crushed stone with high interparticle friction, which value most accurately represents the material's angle of repose?
n: Dry, angular crushed stone with high interparticle friction stands at a steep angle of repose, about 40–45°. Rounded sand and gravel rest at about 30–35°. Source: Das, Principles of Geotechnical Engineering (angle of repose of granular soils); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 1.

q: Standard rebar lengths
n: Reinforcing bars in the Philippines are supplied in standard commercial lengths of 6.0, 7.5, 9.0, 10.5 and 12.0 m. Source: PNS 49:2002 (Steel Bars for Concrete Reinforcement); Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate.

q: What is used to support steel rebars in the formwork of a reinforced concrete beam?
n: A bolster is a continuous wire bar support that holds rebars at the correct height and cover inside beam and slab forms. Source: CRSI Manual of Standard Practice (Bar Supports); ACI 315.

q: A Class A concrete mixture is
n: The Class A mix is 1:2:4 (cement : sand : gravel), giving about 3,000 psi (21 MPa). Class AA is 1:1.5:3, Class B 1:2.5:5, and Class C 1:3:6. Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Concrete Proportion); DPWH Standard Specifications, Item 405.

q: When is the most important period of curing concrete for it to improve strength and durability?
n: The first 7 days are the most critical for curing. Hydration and strength gain are fastest then, and early drying causes plastic shrinkage cracks and permanent strength loss. Source: ACI 308R (Guide to External Curing of Concrete); Kosmatka et al., Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures (PCA), Ch. 12.

q: A contractor in Manila is casting multiple reinforced concrete columns during peak summer conditions, where daytime temperatures regularly exceed 33°C and humidity remains high. The project follows a fast-track schedule, requiring the same set of steel column forms to be reused for the next level as soon as safely possible. The concrete mix uses ordinary Portland cement, no early loads will be applied, and the elevated summer heat accelerates initial hydration. Under these conditions, when is it most appropriate to strip the column formwork?
n: Vertical forms of columns and walls carry no load and may be stripped after 1–2 days. In hot weather with ordinary Portland cement, about 24 hours is enough. Source: ACI 347R (Guide to Formwork for Concrete), Sec. 3.7 (Removal of Forms); NSCP 2015, Sec. 426.

q: Which cement is best suited for places susceptible to chloride or sulfate attack, such as substructures, bored piles and marine structures, and for water-retaining structures such as retaining walls, ports and tunnels, for improved impermeability? It continues to gain strength after the 28-day period and is known to double its strength over 10 to 12 years.
n: Portland blast-furnace slag cement (GGBFS) resists chloride and sulfate attack and has low permeability. It keeps gaining strength well beyond 28 days, which suits piles, marine works and water-retaining structures. Source: ASTM C595 (Blended Hydraulic Cements); ACI 233R (Slag Cement in Concrete).

q: What filler is used at slab-on-grade construction joints?
n: Construction and isolation joints in slabs on grade commonly use premolded bituminous fiber filler. It is compressible, rot-resistant and cheap. Source: ASTM D1751 (Preformed Bituminous Expansion Joint Filler); ACI 302.1R.

q: What is a good replacement for steel rebars on a large area of a slab on grade if ready-mix concrete is used?
n: Welded wire reinforcement (mesh) is the usual replacement for loose rebars in large slab-on-grade pours. It controls shrinkage cracking and is fast to lay. Source: ACI 360R (Design of Slabs-on-Ground); Wire Reinforcement Institute (WRI) manuals.
